A preservative that stops mold and yeast, especially in acidic products.

spotlight.name: Triethylene glycol
spotlight.note: Sprayed into the air to kill some airborne germs. It's also used to dry out natural gas in pipelines.

ingredients.g: Table salt.
A salt that controls thickness and helps keep a liquid stable.
A salt that melts ice at colder temperatures than table salt.
A salt substitute that tastes similar to table salt.
Added color. The label doesn't say which dye.

spotlight.name: Calcium chloride
spotlight.note: It actually heats up as it dissolves, so it melts ice fast. It can also dry out and crack pets' paws.

ingredients.g: Plain water. When it's first on a label, it's the biggest ingredient.
A bright white mineral powder used to make things look whiter.
A plastic-like polymer that forms a film as it dries.
Chalk or ground limestone.
A fine white clay that adds body and helps cover the wall.
A syrupy liquid that dissolves other ingredients and holds in moisture.
A sharp-smelling chemical that adjusts the paint's pH.
A preservative that stops mold and bacteria. The label doesn't say which one.

spotlight.name: Titanium dioxide
spotlight.note: The bright white in white paint — the same mineral used to whiten toothpaste and candy coatings.

puzzles.id: tp|Most toilet paper starts out as trees.
puzzles.statement: Most toilet paper starts out as trees.
puzzles.explain: Most rolls are made from wood pulp, much of it from virgin forests. Bamboo and recycled paper are the main alternatives.

puzzles.statement: Toilet paper is naturally white.
puzzles.explain: Wood pulp is brown. Toilet paper is bleached to make it white — usually with chlorine dioxide.

puzzles.id: tp|Scientists have found PFAS "forever chemicals" in toilet paper.
puzzles.statement: Scientists have found PFAS "forever chemicals" in toilet paper.
puzzles.explain: A 2023 study tested toilet paper from around the world and found PFAS in it. PFAS can be used in paper-making.

puzzles.id: tp|Recycled toilet paper can contain traces of BPA.
puzzles.statement: Recycled toilet paper can contain traces of BPA.
puzzles.explain: BPA coats many thermal cash-register receipts. When receipts get recycled into paper, traces can carry over.

puzzles.id: tp|"Flushable" wipes break down in pipes just like toilet paper.
puzzles.statement: "Flushable" wipes break down in pipes just like toilet paper.
puzzles.explain: Toilet paper is made to fall apart in water within seconds. Wipes hold together, so they clog pipes and sewers.

puzzles.id: tp|Toilet paper is designed to fall apart when it gets wet.
puzzles.statement: Toilet paper is designed to fall apart when it gets wet.
puzzles.explain: Its fibers are short and only lightly bonded, so it breaks up in water instead of clogging your pipes.

puzzles.id: tp|Packaged toilet paper has been sold in the US since the 1850s.
puzzles.statement: Packaged toilet paper has been sold in the US since the 1850s.
puzzles.explain: Joseph Gayetty sold flat sheets of "medicated paper" in 1857. Rolls came a few decades later.

puzzles.id: tp|Most people in the world use toilet paper.
puzzles.statement: Most people in the world use toilet paper.
puzzles.explain: Much of the world — including large parts of Asia, the Middle East and southern Europe — mainly uses water instead.

puzzles.id: tp|The average American uses more than 100 rolls of toilet paper a year.
puzzles.statement: The average American uses more than 100 rolls of toilet paper a year.
puzzles.explain: Estimates put it around 140 rolls per person per year — among the highest in the world.

puzzles.id: tp|Brown, unbleached toilet paper is dirtier than white toilet paper.
puzzles.statement: Brown, unbleached toilet paper is dirtier than white toilet paper.
puzzles.explain: The color comes from skipping the bleach, not from dirt. Unbleached paper just skips a chemical step.

puzzles.id: tp|Scented toilet paper can irritate sensitive skin.
puzzles.statement: Scented toilet paper can irritate sensitive skin.
puzzles.explain: Added fragrance is one of the most common causes of skin irritation, and toilet paper touches very sensitive skin.

puzzles.id: tp|The original 1891 toilet-roll patent drawing shows the paper hanging "over," not "under."
puzzles.statement: The original 1891 toilet-roll patent drawing shows the paper hanging "over," not "under."
puzzles.explain: Seth Wheeler's patent drawing shows the loose end hanging over the front of the roll. Debate settled?

puzzles.id: tp|A 1930s toilet paper brand advertised itself as "splinter-free."
puzzles.statement: A 1930s toilet paper brand advertised itself as "splinter-free."
puzzles.explain: Early paper could contain bits of wood. One brand made "splinter-free" a selling point in the 1930s.

puzzles.id: tp|Most toilet paper sold in the US is made from recycled paper.
puzzles.statement: Most toilet paper sold in the US is made from recycled paper.
puzzles.explain: Most US toilet paper is made from new (virgin) wood pulp. Recycled rolls are a small share of sales.

puzzles.id: tp|Toilet paper sheets have gotten smaller over the years.
puzzles.statement: Toilet paper sheets have gotten smaller over the years.
puzzles.explain: Many brands have quietly shrunk sheet sizes and sheet counts while keeping the price the same.

puzzles.id: tp|Bamboo toilet paper is always chemical-free.
puzzles.statement: Bamboo toilet paper is always chemical-free.
puzzles.explain: Bamboo still has to be pulped and is often bleached. Testers have even found PFAS markers in some bamboo brands.

puzzles.id: tp|In March 2020, US toilet paper sales more than doubled in some weeks.
puzzles.statement: In March 2020, US toilet paper sales more than doubled in some weeks.
puzzles.explain: Panic buying at the start of the pandemic sent sales soaring for weeks and emptied store shelves.

puzzles.id: tp|"Two-ply" means two layers of paper pressed together.
puzzles.statement: "Two-ply" means two layers of paper pressed together.
puzzles.explain: Each sheet is two thin layers bonded together, which makes it softer and stronger than one thick layer.

puzzles.id: tp|Ancient Romans used a sponge on a stick instead of toilet paper.
puzzles.statement: Ancient Romans used a sponge on a stick instead of toilet paper.
puzzles.explain: It was called a tersorium — a sea sponge on a stick, rinsed in water or vinegar and shared.

puzzles.id: tp|Toilet paper companies must list the chemicals used to make it.
puzzles.statement: Toilet paper companies must list the chemicals used to make it.
puzzles.explain: There's no ingredient label on toilet paper. Makers don't have to disclose what goes into it.
